findings.title: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential bypasses custom UserStorageProvider.getCredentials() implementations
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` looks up recovery codes by calling `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()` and falling back to `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)`. `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` only queries `session.userFederatedStorage()` (Keycloak's built-in federated storage table), whereas `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream` queries both local storage and `UserStorageProvider.getCredentials(...)`. However, in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest`, `UserModel` extends `AbstractUserAdapterFederatedStorage`, where `credentialManager().getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)` delegates to `getFederatedCredentialsStream(...)` unless the provider implements `getCredentials`. More importantly, if a user has recovery codes in both federated storage and local storage, or if a `UserStorageProvider` does not use `userFederatedStorage()` and does not override `getCredentials()` to return a full `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` (for instance, a legacy storage provider that only implements `CredentialInputUpdater` and `CredentialInputValidator` as in Keycloak 4.8.3), `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` will return `Optional.empty()`. In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` (line 19), `credentialModelOpt.get()` is called unconditionally without checking `isPresent()`, which will throw `NoSuchElementException` when rendering the recovery code login form for such a provider, and in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (line 90), `recoveryCodeCredentialModel == null` will force `CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES` after a single login.

findings.title: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage overrides getCredentials, breaking its 4.8.3 backwards-compatibility contract
findings.body: The class-level Javadoc of `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` states: "UserStorage implementation created in Keycloak 4.8.3. It is used for backwards compatibility testing. Future Keycloak versions should work fine without a need to change the code of this provider." `CredentialInputValidator.getCredentials(RealmModel, UserModel)` did not exist in Keycloak 4.8.3 (it was added much later as a default method returning `Stream.empty()`). By overriding `getCredentials` and using `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`, the test no longer verifies backwards compatibility with a 4.8.3-style `CredentialInputUpdater`/`CredentialInputValidator` implementation, and masks the `NoSuchElementException` in `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` when `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` returns `Optional.empty()`.
